title: Review: Water; Elements, monomers and condensation/hydrolysis; Polysaccharides; Monosaccharides and disaccharides
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for AP Biology (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: BM04#t2 term and clue written for the game; BM02#t2 term and clue written for the game; BM02#t3 term and clue written for the game; BM03#t2 term and clue written for the game. Questions: BM01a#N.5b, BM01b#N.7b, BM02#N.8b, BM03#N.7b, BM04#N.12, BM01a#N.10, BM01b#N.4c, BM02#N.10b, BM01a#N.4b, BM01b#N.15b. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Glycogen
items.clue: The energy store found in animals and fungi

items.label: Polymer
items.clue: A large molecule made of many small units joined together

items.label: Condensation
items.clue: Joining reaction that releases one water molecule for each bond formed

items.label: Isomers
items.clue: Molecules such as glucose and fructose: same atoms, arranged differently

questions.stem: The model shows three water molecules. The symbols δ+ and δ− show partial charges. Which statement correctly describes the interaction labelled 2 in the model?

options.text: An attraction between the partially positive H of one molecule and the partially negative O of another
A covalent bond in which the H atom of one molecule shares a pair of electrons with the O atom of another
An ionic bond between an H⁺ ion in one molecule and an O²⁻ ion in a second, neighbouring molecule
A strong bond, stronger than line 1, that holds the two water molecules in a fixed position

questions.stem: Consider three observations: (1) the temperature of a large lake changes little between day and night; (2) sweat evaporating from the skin cools the body; (3) small insects can walk on the surface of a pond without sinking. Which statement best explains what the three observations have in common?

options.text: Each depends on covalent bonds that keep forming and breaking between water molecules.
Each depends on ionic bonds between the H⁺ ions and O²⁻ ions that make up water.
Each depends on hydrogen bonds that form between neighbouring polar water molecules.
Each depends on the bonds that hold the H atoms to the O atom inside every water molecule.

questions.stem: In a cell, one reaction builds a polymer from monomers while another reaction breaks a different polymer into its monomers. Which statement correctly compares the role of water in the two reactions?

options.text: Building the polymer uses water; breaking the other polymer down releases water.
Building the polymer releases water; breaking the other one down uses water.
Building the polymer uses water, and breaking the other polymer down also uses water.
Neither reaction uses or releases water; in both, water serves only as the solvent.

questions.explanation: Dehydration synthesis releases the equivalent of one water molecule per bond formed; hydrolysis uses one water molecule per bond broken.

questions.stem: Which statement correctly describes the relationship between monosaccharides and polysaccharides?

options.text: A polysaccharide is a polymer of many monosaccharides joined to one another by covalent bonds.
A polysaccharide is many monosaccharides held to one another by hydrogen bonds, not covalent bonds.
A polysaccharide is just one long, unbranched chain of monosaccharides joined end to end.
Polysaccharides are carbohydrates, but monosaccharides are simple sugars and not carbohydrates.

questions.explanation: Monosaccharides (simple sugars) are the monomers of polysaccharides (complex carbohydrates); each unit is joined to the next by a covalent bond formed by dehydration synthesis.

questions.stem: The model represents one molecule of a branched polysaccharide. Each hexagon is one monosaccharide unit, and each line joining two hexagons is a bond between them. How many water molecules are used when this molecule is hydrolysed completely into monosaccharides?
questions.explanation: 20 units are joined by 19 bonds: 11 along the main row, 3 within each side chain, and 1 attaching each side chain to the row. One water per bond.

questions.stem: In blood plasma, glucose travels freely dissolved. Cholesterol does not: it travels inside lipoprotein particles whose outer surface carries polar and charged groups. Why does cholesterol need this carrier?

options.text: Cholesterol molecules are too large to fit between water molecules and dissolve.
Water molecules push cholesterol away with a repulsive force between them.
Cholesterol is largely non-polar, so it forms few attractions with water.
Glucose splits into ions in water, but cholesterol stays as whole molecules.

questions.explanation: With almost no δ+ or δ− regions, cholesterol cannot hydrogen-bond with water; it is hydrophobic. The carrier's polar, charged surface is attracted to water and carries the cholesterol through the plasma.

questions.stem: The model shows water molecules next to the surface of a glass tube; the glass surface carries polar O–H groups. Dashed lines show attractions between molecules. Which property of water is represented by the attractions labelled 1?

options.text: Cohesion, the attraction of water molecules to a substance that is not water
Surface tension, the pull of water toward the walls of the container holding it
Adhesion, the attraction of water molecules to the molecules of a different polar substance
Covalent bonding, in which water molecules share pairs of electrons with the glass

questions.explanation: Lines 1 are hydrogen bonds between the glass's O–H groups and water molecules: attraction to a different substance is adhesion. Lines 2, between water molecules, show cohesion.

questions.stem: In a cell, 10 molecules of a hypothetical monomer, each with a molar mass of 180 g/mol, are joined into one unbranched chain by dehydration synthesis. The molar mass of water is 18 g/mol. What is the molar mass of the polymer formed?

options.text: 1800 g/mol
1620 g/mol
1638 g/mol
1962 g/mol

questions.stem: In a water molecule, each of the two hydrogen atoms is joined to the oxygen atom by a covalent bond. Which statement best explains why a water molecule is polar?

options.text: Each H atom transfers its electron completely to the O atom, so the molecule consists of ions of opposite charge.
Hydrogen bonds inside the molecule join each H atom to the O atom, and these bonds give the atoms their charges.
The molecule picks up extra electrons from its surroundings, so as a whole it carries a negative charge.
O attracts the shared electrons more strongly than H, so O is partially negative and each H partially positive.

questions.stem: Dogs lose little heat by sweating. On a hot day a dog pants: air moves quickly over its wet tongue and airways. How does panting cool the dog?

options.text: Moving air cools any surface, so a dry tongue would cool the dog just as well.
Heat from the tongue breaks the O–H bonds inside the water molecules there.
Breaking the hydrogen bonds releases energy, which the vapour then carries away.
Evaporating molecules must break hydrogen bonds, taking heat from the tongue.

questions.explanation: Water's high heat of vaporisation means each gram that evaporates removes about 2400 J from the tongue and airways: a large cooling effect for little water lost.
